title: COSMOS: Performance Portable Graph Pattern Matching with Domain-Specific Software Distributed Shared Memory
problem: Graph pattern matching (GPM) is NP-complete and irregular in nature, making it difficult to scale to distributed systems on complex supercomputers. Architecture-specific optimizations lack portability and cause vendor lock-in.
motivation: Enable the same GPM code to scale across thousands of nodes on different supercomputers without manual re-optimization, achieving both performance portability and competitive performance.
method: The system uses a software layer called distributed shared memory (DSM)—a unified memory view across multiple networked computers—customized for graph pattern matching problems. This layer automatically adapts the same code to run efficiently on different supercomputer configurations, whether they have different processors, GPUs, or memory systems. It handles the complexity of coordinating work across many computers while hiding the specific details of each machine's hardware.
key_novelty: A software layer (distributed shared memory) designed for graph pattern matching that lets the same code run across different supercomputers while matching the speed of hand-tuned versions built for each specific machine.
contributions: Domain-specific distributed shared memory model for graph pattern matching
Performance-portable GPM implementation across diverse supercomputer architectures
Demonstration of scaling to thousands of nodes without code rewrite
limitations: Abstract lacks specific performance numbers or comparison baselines
primary_theme: Performance Portability in Distributed Graph Processing
